findings.reason: without a scoped or followupped declaration no project will ever name a server, so §11's premise ("the opt-in half is inert") survives its own landing.
findings.text: §11 names "imas-codex ... declares imas-cx there in its flight configuration" as part of the solution, but imas-codex has no flight config (`docs/state/imas-codex/flight.yaml` absent; its repo is outside §11's write paths of `reckon/flight.py` and the test), no followup records the change, and §11's live done-when checks an imas-ambix worktree (snapshot:231) — a project that declares no server, so the check passes on the unfixed code — meaning the section can close green while §7's opt-in half stays inert in production, the exact condition §11 exists to fix

findings.reason: §3/§4/§6/§7 landed after this followup was authored and the plan's own state-integrity rule requires the driving followup be refreshed when work lands, so the section-to-wave wiring a coordinator dispatches from is out of date.
findings.text: the only followup, f-amfc-001, is `open` and its body states "§2, §3, §4 and §6 ... can run together" although §3/§4/§6 have since landed, and it names neither §8/§9/§10 nor §11, so the plan's declared next invocation (`/reckon-build an-mcp-failure-names-its-cause`) carries a coordination note that is stale and incomplete for the current remaining wave

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `mounts.json` maps each project to `<checkout>/docs`, so §5's "repository that holds the mount's docs/ directory" resolves (imas-codex → /home/ITER/mcintos/Code/imas-codex, whose `.mcp.json` exists); the four evidence anchors in §3/§4/§6/§7 resolve to ids in `docs/evidence/archive/an-mcp-failure-names-its-cause-landed.html`; `/reckon/reckon-reads-answer-in-seconds` and both §11 test/module paths resolve.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §5's fixture and its two negative controls are internally consistent (three flags on the user-scope entry now that the missing-directory rule fires on `/home/someone/Code/reckon`), and §11 carries a falsifiable unit test with a reverted-schema negative control.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §11's `ps` listing is written to the run directory (snapshot:231); §5's gate is a test whose red log the run manifest records, and its test-isolation rule (temporary home, real `~/.claude.json` untouched) is stated (snapshot:150-152).
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or version tags reach any symbol, file or comment named by the changed units.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §11's stated production outcome (the opt-in half is no longer inert) requires a project to declare `worker_mcp_servers`, but §11 scopes no write path or followup for the imas-codex declaration it names, and its live check targets imas-ambix, which declares nothing.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each changed section names one deliverable: §5 a doctor launch check, §11 the schema admission of `worker_mcp_servers`.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — the driving followup f-amfc-001 (snapshot:249) still describes §3/§4/§6 as a pending wave and never names §8/§9/§10/§11, so the plan's declared next invocation omits four implementable sections and the §11→§7 relationship.
